thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: STREAMING_LATENCY_SLO_BREACH triggered in #prod-streaming. p95 jumped from 1.8s -> 3.9s, p99 from 5.2s -> 12.4s over the last 5m. Affected endpoints: /v1/stream/chat, /v1/stream/generate. Suspected streaming stalls / chunking delays. Severity: Sev2. Paging @manny and @jordan.

manny (oncall): on it. I’m pulling traces + recent deploys. Any customer-visible errors? Sasha, can you flag any support cases?

sasha (support): we’ve got 2 customers reporting “responses stalled then all at once” on chat streaming since ~10:02Z. No HTTP 5xx observed. Browser console logs show large gaps between SSE chunks.

jordan (eng-runtime): I’m seeing spikes in write latency at the proxy layer. Upstream writes to websocket buffer are q'ing. Looking at host twr-gw-12: netstat shows many connections in ESTABLISHED with backpressure on socket write.

alice (eng-sre): grabbing metrics. Streaming proxy (gw) p99 write latency: 89ms -> 1.1s in last 10m. Kernel send buffer full events increased. Also noticed increase in client-slow-consumer count.

manny (oncall): reproduce plan: 1) Check recent routing changes / deploys 2) Enable aggressive chunk-flush on streaming adapter 3) Fallback routing to dedicated low-latency model variant if stall persists 4) Notify customers.

dev (eng-platform): No deploys in last hour. Autoscaler did bump some instances ~10:00Z. No config rollouts.

jordan (eng-runtime): quick dump of proxy backpressure counters:

```
# tcp_write_blocked_total
host twr-gw-12: 362
host twr-gw-13: 310
host twr-gw-14: 28
```
Also observed long syscalls in accept/sendfile path. Suspect slow consumers at client side + proxy buffering policy mismatch.

alice (eng-sre): mitigation attempt 1: lowering proxy max_buffer_size to 128KB on twr-gw-12/13 to force earlier flushes. Applying as a hotfix now.

incidents-bot: Action logged: config change initiated by alice @ 1748054410.

manny (oncall): rolled on twr-gw-12/13. Monitoring p95/p99. Please hold off wider roll until we confirm behavior.

(2m later)

jordan (eng-runtime): After buffer changes, p95 improved from 3.9s -> 2.1s. p99 still high ~9.8s. Saw several clients with receive window zero for >30s (client-side slow consumers).

lee (customer-success): Notifying affected customers with interim update: short blurb on symptoms and that we’ve implemented proxy flush change and are routing around the slowest consumers.

sasha (support): Customers asking: Are messages lost? Answer: No, messages buffered server-side and delivered but with bursty experience.

manny (oncall): Mitigation attempt 2: enable fallback routing for streaming to model-variant: rwdx-small-fast for customers on hosted tier to reduce per-token processing latency and reduce end-to-end tail. Triggering now for 10% of traffic on /v1/stream/* routes.

incidents-bot: Rollout started: fallback variant rwdx-small-fast, 10% traffic @ 1748054605.

jordan (eng-runtime): Observing immediate drop in CPU per-request on fallback. p95 -> 1.4s for rolled traffic. Non-rolled traffic still p99 ~8-10s.

alice (eng-sre): Additional step: increased keepalive timeout on gw from 30s -> 60s to reduce premature socket closes causing retransmit spikes. Also tightened upstream idle flush interval to 100ms.

manny (oncall): Can we throttle aggressive clients? Any rate-limiter we can apply to slow consumers?

dev (eng-platform): We have a soft throttle on write queue per-conn. I can add a temporary eviction for connections exceeding 120s of blocked writes. Pushing change as emergency flag.

(5m later)

jordan (eng-runtime): After eviction toggle, number of blocked connections dropped 75%. p99 decreased to ~4.6s. Looks promising.

lee (customer-success): Customers confirming improvement: behavior is back to normal for most. Still one enterprise customer seeing intermittent bursts — they have a flaky mobile proxy.

manny (oncall): Summary of mitigations applied: 
- lowered proxy buffer to 128KB on affected nodes
- enabled fallback model variant for 10% traffic
- increased keepalive and decreased upstream flush interval
- enabled blocked-connection eviction after 120s

incidents-bot: Incident state: mitigation in place, SLO delta reduced. Continue monitoring for 30m. Assigning owner for post-incident: jordan (eng-runtime).

jordan (eng-runtime): I’ll own postmortem and action items. Next steps: collect tcpdump from affected gw nodes, get client-side traces from the one remaining enterprise customer, investigate kernel socket backlog tuning and consider proactive autoscaling thresholds for streaming heavy routes.

alice (eng-sre): Action items I’ll take: add more granular metric for per-connection blocked-write-time, alert at 30s blocked threshold; run a canary with reduced buffer on non-prod to validate default config; document emergency evacuation steps for slow consumers.

manny (oncall): Handoff: I need to go offline in ~20m. Jordan, take lead for night watch. If anything re-escalates to Sev1 (sustained p99 > 10s coupled with >10 customers impacted), please page me.

jordan (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. I’ll keep the rollback knobs ready and update on-call notes.

sasha (support): Sending final customer update now: short explanation + what we changed + ETA for postmortem.

lee (customer-success): I’ll close the open support tickets once they confirm stable for 30m.

manny (oncall): closing thread here and attaching runbook/links in the incident tracker. Great cross-team work. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Incident logged as STREAMING_LATENCY_SLO_BREACH-1748054321. Postmortem owner: jordan. Next steps: postmortem due in 72h.
